author: ValWood
body:
GO:0052851 | ferric-chelate reductase (NADPH) activity | IEA with 28795 | GO_REF:0000116

https://www.pombase.org/gene/SPBC947.05c
and
https://www.pombase.org/gene/SPBC1683.09c

In fission yeast, these aren't 
Catalysis of the reaction: 2 Fe3+-siderophore + NADP+ + H+ -> 2 Fe2+-siderophore + NADPH.


but rather 
https://www.rhea-db.org/rhea/71767
see
https://github.com/geneontology/go-ontology/issues/27593

ALthough pombe does make siderophore (ferrichrome), this is part of the siderophore independent system for iron uptake.


Expert says:
However, there is no evidence that this happens in S. pombe,
In nature, people believe that Fe3+ is extracted from ferric oxyhydroxide (and other similar compounds)
more accurate to indicate
2 Fe3+ + NADP+ + H+ -> 2 Fe2 + NADPH
